renders._yaml:
- component: card
  title: Haploid genome length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over read sets of GenomeScope's upper estimate of the haploid genome length, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how large the genome is expected to be before any assembly.
    How to read: an assembly total close to this length is complete in size. A total well above it suggests duplicated haplotypes, and one well below suggests missing sequence. Read sets that disagree point to different genomes or to poor fits.
  column: haploid_length_max
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: upper estimate per read set, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Heterozygosity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over read sets of GenomeScope's upper estimate of heterozygosity, as a percentage of the genome, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much the two haplotypes differ.
    How to read: a high value warns that a collapsed assembly will carry duplicated haplotigs and may need purging. A value near zero means the haplotypes are almost identical.
  column: heterozygosity_max
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: upper estimate per read set, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Repeat content
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over read sets of the share of the genome that GenomeScope places in repeats, in percent, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how repetitive the genome is.
    How to read: a high share makes short-read assembly harder and favours long reads. Treat it as an estimate of the k-mer model, not a count of annotated repeats.
  column: repeat_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: share of the genome, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Model fit
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest model fit over read sets, in percent, and the box shows the spread of the upper fit estimates. It answers whether the numbers of this tab can be trusted.
    How to read: a high fit means the model follows the observed k-mer spectrum. A poor fit usually means too little coverage or too much sequencing error, and then the other estimates are unreliable. GenomeScope recommends at least 15x coverage of the haploid genome.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tbenavi1/genomescope2.0/master/README.md
  column: model_fit_max
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: best fit per read set, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Estimated haploid genome length per read set
  description: |-
    Each bar is a read set: GenomeScope's upper estimate of its haploid genome length, coloured by its estimated heterozygosity. It answers whether the read sets agree on the genome size.
    How to read: similar bars mean the reads sample the same genome. A bar that stands out, especially with a different heterozygosity, may come from a different organism, a contaminated library or a poor fit, so compare it with the model fit card.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median haploid genome length of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of GenomeScope.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: read_set
    y: haploid_length_max
    color: heterozygosity_max
    labels:
      read_set: Read set
      haploid_length_max: Haploid genome length (bp)
      heterozygosity_max: Heterozygosity (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: haploid_length_max

- component: table
  title: GenomeScope estimates
  description: |-
    Each row is a read set, with GenomeScope's lower and upper estimates of genome length, repeat length, heterozygosity, read error rate and model fit. It answers what range each number was fitted to.
    How to read: the gap between the minimum and maximum columns is the uncertainty of the fit, so a wide gap means the estimate is loose.
